s: Name as indexed in a chain
as: أحد العشرة وأول من رمى بسهم في سبيل الله ومناقبه كثيرة
One of the Ten, the first to shoot an arrow in God’s cause, and credited with many merits.
وكان أحد الفرسان الشجعان من قريش، الذين كانوا يحرسون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مغازيه
He was one of the courageous Quraysh cavalrymen who guarded the Messenger of God on his campaigns.
إن وليها سعد فذاك، وإلا فليستعن به الوالي، فإني لم أعزله عن عجز ولا خيانة.
If Saʿd rules, so be it. Otherwise let the ruler seek his help. I dismissed him neither for inability nor for treachery.
أولئك قوم خذلوا الحق ولم ينصروا الباطل
Those men failed to help the right and gave no support to the wrong. This is reported as ʿAlī’s judgment on those who sat out.
He was well known for having his prayers answered.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by al-Mizzī
O God, guide his shot and answer his prayer.
عمر, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
إن أصابت الإمرة سعدا فذاك، وإلا فليستعن به الذي يلي الأمر، فإني لم أعزله عن عجز ولا خيانة.
If Saʿd becomes ruler, so be it. Otherwise let whoever rules seek his help, for I did not dismiss him for inability or treachery.
أبو إسحاق, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
كان أشد أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعة: عمر، وعلي، والزبير، وسعد.
The four staunchest Companions were ʿUmar, ʿAlī, al-Zubayr and Saʿd.
جرير, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
تركته في ولايته أكرم الناس مقدرة وأقلهم قسوة ، هو لهم كالأم البرة، يجمع لهم كما تجمع الذرة، أشد الناس عن الباس، وأحب قريش إلى الناس.

When I left him governing, he was exceedingly generous in power and gentle, caring for the people like a devoted mother and gathering for them as an ant gathers. He was formidable and the Qurashī most beloved to the people.
He was known for having his prayers answered.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
O God, answer Saʿd when he calls upon You.
الزبير, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
عمر, quoted by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr
إن وليها سعد فذاك وإلا فليستعن به الوالي، فإني لم أعزله عن عجز ولا خيانة.
If Saʿd rules, so be it. Otherwise the ruler should seek his help, for I removed him neither for inability nor for treachery.
وكان أحد الفرسان الشجعان من قريش الذين كانوا يحرسون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مغازيه
He was one of the courageous Quraysh cavalrymen who guarded the Messenger of God in his campaigns.
علي, quoted by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr
أولئك قوم خذلوا الحق، ولم ينصروا الباطل
Those men failed to help the right and gave no support to the wrong.
وكان مجاب الدعوة مشهورا بذلك، تخاف دعوته وترجى، لا يشك في إجابتها عندهم
He was known for answered prayers. People feared or hoped for his prayers and were sure they would be answered.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr
O God, guide his arrow and answer his prayer.
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, quoted by Ibn al-Athīr
إن ولي سعد الإمارة فذاك، وإلا فأوصي الخليفة بعدي أن يستعمله، فإني لم أعزله من عجز ولا خيانة
If Saʿd takes office, so be it. Otherwise I advise my successor to employ him, for I did not dismiss him on account of incapacity or treachery.
عمرو بن معديكرب, quoted by Ibn al-Athīr
متواضع في خبائه، عربي في نمرته ، أسد في تاموره، يعدل في القضية، ويقسم بالسوية، ويبعد في السرية، ويعطف علينا عطف الأم البرة، وينقل إلينا حقنا نقل الذرة .
Humble in his tent, Arab in his cloak, and a lion in his den. He judges fairly, divides equally, ventures far in expeditions, cares for us like a devoted mother, and brings our due like an ant.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn al-Athīr
O God, answer Saʿd when he calls upon You.
عبد الله, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
لقد رأيت سعدا يقاتل يوم بدر قتال الفارس في الرجال.
I saw Saʿd fight at Badr as a horseman fights among men.
السائب بن يزيد, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
فما سمعته يحدث عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - حديثا حتى رجع.
On their journey, al-Sāʾib heard him narrate no hadith from the Prophet until he returned.
وكان من الرماة المذكورين من أصحاب رسول الله
He was one of the noted archers among the Companions of the Messenger of God.
علي بن أبو طالب, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
ما سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يفدي أحدا بأبويه إلا سعدا فإني سمعته يقول يوم أحد: ارم سعد فداك أبي وأمي
I heard the Messenger offer both parents as ransom for Saʿd alone. At Uḥud he said, ‘Shoot, Saʿd. May my father and mother be your ransom.’
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
O God, answer him when he calls upon You.
سعد بن أبو وقاص, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
إني أخاف أن أحدثكم واحدا فتزيدوا عليه المائة
I fear I will tell you one report and you will add a hundred to it.

as: حفاظ الناس ثلاثة: إسماعيل بن أبي خالد، وعبد الملك بن أبي سليمان، ويحيى بن سعيد الأنصاري، وهو، يعني إسماعيل - أعلم الناس بالشعبي. وأثبتهم فيه .
Al-Thawrī names three master transmitters: Ismāʿīl, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī. Ismāʿīl knew al-Shaʿbī best and was his firmest transmitter.
ابن أبي خالد يزدرد العلم ازدرادا.
Ibn Abī Khālid gulped down knowledge.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Both Ibn Abī Khālid and al-Shaybānī were trustworthy.
عبد الرحمن بن مهي, quoted by al-Mizzī
محمد بن عبد الله بن عمار الموصلي, quoted by al-Mizzī
حجة، إذا لم يكن إسماعيل حجة، فمن يكون حجة؟ !
An authority. If Ismāʿīl is not an authority, who would be?
كوفي، تابعي، ثقة، وكان رجلا صالحا، وسمع من خمسة من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وكان طحانا.
A trustworthy Kufan Successor and an upright man. He heard from five Companions and worked as a miller.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
لا أقدم عليه أحدا من أصحاب الشعبي، وهو ثقة، أروى من بيان وفراس ، وأحفظ من مجالد.
I place none of al-Shaʿbī's associates ahead of him. He is trustworthy, transmits more than Bayān and Firās, and has a better memory than Mujālid.
The most knowledgeable of people about al-Shaʿbī and the most precise in transmitting from him.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Ismāʿīl knows al-Shaʿbī better than Ibn ʿAwn.
Yaʿqūb ibn Shaybah, quoted by al-Mizzī
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما حملت عن إسماعيل عن عامر، صحاح؟ قال: نعم.
Asked whether the reports he took from Ismāʿīl on ʿĀmir's authority were sound, Yaḥyā agreed.
Sufyān al-Thawrī, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
الحفاظ عندنا أربعة: عبد الملك بن أبي سليمان وإسماعيل بن أبي خالد وعاصم الأحول ويحيى بن سعيد الأنصاري.
Four among us are hadith masters: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān, Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī.

t2117.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Zayd ibn Aslam al-ʿAdawī, client of ʿUmar, Abū ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Usāma al-Madanī, as trustworthy and a scholar who used to transmit in mursal form, of the third generation; he died in 36.
as: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
لم يسمع من جابر، ولا من أبي هريرة
He did not hear from Jābir or Abū Hurayrah.
محمد بن عجلان, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما هبت أحدا قط هيبتي زيد بن أسلم
I never stood in such awe of anyone as I did of Zayd ibn Aslam.
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Yaʿqūb ibn Shaybah, quoted by al-Mizzī
ثقة من أهل الفقه والعلم، وكان عالما بتفسير القرآن، له كتاب فيه تفسير القرآن
Reliable and among the people of jurisprudence and learning. He was learned in Qurʾān commentary and wrote a book on it.
كان زيد بن أسلم يحدث من تلقاء نفسه، فإذا سكت قام، فلا يجترئ عليه إنسان
Zayd began transmitting of his own accord and stood up when he was finished. No one ventured to press him.
لم يبق أحد أرضى لنفسي وديني غير ذلك
No one remaining satisfies me more for myself and my religion.
فأذكر بالنظر إليه القوة على عبادتك
Looking at him reminds me of the strength to worship You.
يعقوب بن عبد الله بن الأشج, quoted by al-Mizzī
ليس من الخلق أحد أمن علي من زيد بن أسلم
No one has done me a greater favor than Zayd ibn Aslam.
He was reliable and transmitted many hadiths.

t2399.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr ibn Shuʿba, Abū ʿUthmān al-Khurāsānī who settled in Mecca, as trustworthy and a compiler; he would not retract what was in his book. He died in 227, or it is said later, of the tenth generation.
as: Trustworthy and a compiler of works.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
One of the virtuous and truthful.
محمد بن عبد الله بن نمير, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
من المتقنين الأثبات ممن جمع وصنف.
One of the precise and firm transmitters who collected hadith and compiled works.
محمد بن عبد الرحيم, quoted by al-Mizzī
يحيى بن حسان, quoted by al-Mizzī
مقدما لسعيد بن منصور يرى له حفظه
He gave Saʿīd precedence in recognition of his memory.
الحاكم أبو عبد الله, quoted by al-Mizzī
وهو راوية سفيان بن عيينة، وأحد أئمة الحديث، له مصنفات كثيرة متفق على إخراجه في "الصحيحين.
He was a transmitter of Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, one of the leading hadith scholars and an author of many works. Both Ṣaḥīḥs included his transmissions.
يعقوب بن سفيان, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان إذا في كتابه خطأ لم يرجع عنه.
When there was an error in his book, he would not retract it.
حرب بن إسماعيل, quoted by al-Mizzī
وأملى علينا نحوا من عشرة آلاف حديث من حفظه، ثم صنف بعد ذلك الكتب وكان موسعا عليه.
He dictated roughly ten thousand hadiths to us from memory. He later compiled books and was well provided for.
وعبد الرحمن بنيوسف بن خراش, quoted by al-Mizzī

t7051.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Maymūn, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Baṣrī, client of Ibn Samura, as weak, of the fourth generation; it is said his father's name is Ustādh, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim distinguished between them.

t7275.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records al-Hurmuzān as a mukhaḍram of the second generation who accepted Islam at ʿUmar's hands and was killed the day ʿUmar was killed; a mawqūf report from him appears in al-Bukhārī.

t728.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Bashir, who transmitted from Ibn al-Zubayr, unknown, of the fourth generation.

t7349.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Hilāl ibn Abī Hilāl or Ibn Abī Mālik, i.e. Ibn Maymūn, Abū Ḍilāl al-Qasmalī al-Baṣrī, as weak and well known by his kunya, of the fifth generation; his father's name is disputed.
as: weak, well known by his kunya

t7419.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records al-Walīd ibn Jamīl al-Filasṭīnī, known as Abū al-Ḥajjāj, as truthful but making mistakes, belonging to the sixth generation.

t7503.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Yaḥyā ibn Abī Umāma Asʿad ibn Zurāra al-Anṣārī al-Madanī as a young Companion who has a hadith.

t7608.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Yaḥyā ibn ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr al-Asadī, Abū ʿUrwa al-Madanī, as trustworthy, of the sixth generation.

t7936.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists Abū Isḥāq al-Dawsī, client of the Hāshimites, as acceptable and of the third generation, noting he may be the one before him.

t8021.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Abū Jaʿfar al-Qāriʾ al-Madanī al-Makhzūmī, named Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ or Jundub ibn Fayrūz, as trustworthy, of the fourth generation, dying in year twenty-seven or year thirty; cited by Abū Dāwūd.

t8245.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records that Abū ʿUthmān, teacher of al-Awzāʿī, is unknown, of the sixth generation; Abū Dāwūd said he thought he was Jisr ibn al-Ḥasan.
as: I think he is Jisr ibn al-Ḥasan

t8443.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists another Abū Yaḥyā al-Taymī al-Madanī, named Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh, abandoned, of the eighth generation, and marks it as a distinguishing note.

t8559.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Ḥabība bint Maysara al-Fihriyya as acceptable (maqbūla) and belonging to the fourth generation.

t8696.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Hind bint al-Ḥārith al-Khathʿamiyyah, acceptable, also of the third generation, marked as a distinguishing entry.

t953.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Hudhayl al-Kūfī, grandson of Abū Usāma, as trustworthy and a man of hadith, of the eleventh generation, who died in 60 AH.
